question: Are pre-square buys that come just after a fresh peak, with the slow %R rolling over, worse than other buys?

pattern_AFTER_PEAK (fixed, no tuning).peak: the highest high of the 10 minutes before the signal bar was 2-8 minutes ago
pattern_AFTER_PEAK (fixed, no tuning).lower: the signal bar's close is >= 10 bp below that high
pattern_AFTER_PEAK (fixed, no tuning).slow_roll: slow %R (112, EWM 3) at the signal bar minus 2 bars ago <= 0, AND slow %R 3 bars ago minus 8 bars ago > 0 (it was rising, now flat or falling)

data: the desk's live pre-square arm on SIP minute bars (evening_family.presquare_bars, fast %R 21, refractory 30, minutes 15-360), top-400 universe, $20-$400, up >= 1.5% at the signal bar, every warehouse day with SPY; trade open t+1 -> close t+10, 6 bp; straight-down = low over t+1..t+10 <= open - 40 bp

pass_if_ALL.size: AFTER_PEAK mean net - other signals' mean net <= -3.0 bp
pass_if_ALL.significance: day-clustered t of the per-day difference <= -2.0
pass_if_ALL.both_halves: the difference is negative in the first and second half of the days
pass_if_ALL.kept_quality: skipping AFTER_PEAK raises the kept signals' mean above all signals' mean

after_pass: a live arm refusal behind a switch (default off) computed from the desk's own 1-minute bars; ships (paper) under the operator's 11/18 rule
caveats: minute bars with a fixed 10-minute exit; the live arm fires on 10-second polls, the pattern is judged at the signal bar's close
